utterances.speaker: Lisa
utterances.text: Hi David, hi Emma, thanks for making the time. Alex Martin from our product team is with me today.

utterances.speaker: David
utterances.text: Thanks Lisa, Emma from our IT department joins us too, she will handle the integration on our side.

utterances.speaker: Emma
utterances.text: Hello everyone.

utterances.speaker: Alex Martin
utterances.text: Hi both. So, the goal today is to go through your requirements for the rollout and decree on the plan. David, do you want to start with what matters most for you?

utterances.speaker: David
utterances.text: Sure, three things. First, single sign on with our Microsoft accounts, that's a must for our security team. Second, an export of the reports to Excel. And third, we need to go live on December 1st, because our new financial year starts then.

utterances.speaker: Alex Martin
utterances.text: Okay. The Excel export is easy, we already have it in beta. Single sign-on is more work. With your Azure setup I estimate 6 to 8 weeks. 6

utterances.speaker: David
utterances.text: Six to eight weeks, then we would miss December 1st.

utterances.speaker: Alex Martin
utterances.text: Yes. What I'd suggest is to go live on December 1st without single sign-on, with normal logins, and add single sign-on in the second phase in January.

utterances.speaker: Emma
utterances.text: From the IT side that could work, if the normal logins use strong passwords and two-factor authentication.

utterances.speaker: Alex Martin
utterances.text: They do. Two factors are by default.

utterances.speaker: David
utterances.text: Then I agree. Phase 1 on December 1st without single sign-on, and single sign-on in January. I need it in writing.

utterances.speaker: Lisa
utterances.text: Of course. I'll send you a revised quote and the statement of work with the two phases by Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: David
utterances.text: Good. About the budget, we have a hard cap of 80,000 euros for this year. The first quote was 85.

utterances.speaker: Lisa
utterances.text: I understand. If single sign-on moves to January, part of the cost moves to next year's budget. I'm confident we can stay under 80,000 for this year.

utterances.speaker: Emma
utterances.text: I have one concern. Our legal team requires that all data stays in the European Union. Where are your servers?

utterances.speaker: Alex Martin
utterances.text: Our main servers are in Frankfurt, so it's fine. But our backup provider is in the US. I need to check if we can move the backups to Europe. I'll confirm that by next Friday.

utterances.speaker: Emma
utterances.text: Thank you, that's important. If backups stay in the US, legal will block the project.

utterances.speaker: David
utterances.text: Also, we want a pilot first. 40 users in the finance team, for two weeks, before the full rollout to the 600 employees.

utterances.speaker: Alex Martin
utterances.text: That's a good idea. Emma, can you send us the list of the 40 pilot users?

utterances.speaker: Emma
utterances.text: Yes, I'll send the list on Monday.

utterances.speaker: Alex Martin
utterances.text: And I'd like to organize a technical workshop with your team next week to prepare the integration. I'll send a few time slots to Emma.

utterances.speaker: David
utterances.text: Perfect. And on my side, I need the legal approval for the data processing agreement. I'll get that signed by November 6th.

utterances.speaker: Lisa
utterances.text: So we have a plan. Thank you both. We'll be in touch this week.
